entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Harmon et al. (1997), Science 278, 1921); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Hyakutake passed just 0.10 AU from Earth in March 1996. Its close approach made it a striking sight despite its much smaller nucleus than Hale–Bopp’s. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Harmon et al. (1997), Science 278, 1921: effective radius 1.25 km. Unresolved; the midpoint of the radar diameter range is displayed as a sphere. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
